correctness.rationale: The direct order-map classification is correct. Maps with the two minima equal, with a maximal image at a minimum-domain point, or with a constant maximal-level restriction are comparable to constants and hence lie in one null component. If the minima are permuted and the maximal-level map is nonconstant, any pointwise comparable self-map must agree coordinatewise, so the map is isolated. Such a map sends a four-edge K_{2,q} cycle with two distinct maximal images to a nonzero four-cycle; because the order complex is one-dimensional there are no 2-boundaries, so H1 action is nonzero. Counting the four order-map forms gives the stated total, isolated and null-component sizes. The frozen q=2,3,4 enumeration independently checks components and H1 action.

originality.rationale: A published SCOPE result, 'Mapping-space decomposition for complete height-two finite models', proves for all p,q,r,s>=2 that |[P_{p,q},P_{r,s}]|=1+(r^p-r)(s^q-s), classifies exactly the isolated maps, gives the total map count, and identifies the homotopy type of the unique nonisolated component. Specializing p=r=2 and source=target P_{2,q} yields the submitted class count 1+2(q^q-q), the same isolated/nonisolated decomposition, and the same total-map formula. The remaining H1 label is a routine graph-homology characterization of those already-classified maps. Thus the submitted final claim is covered by a stronger published result.
